codeReview.summary: The feature correctly implemented key exit-code parity (match/no-match/error/mixed outcomes) and improved invalid-option/invalid-regex handling, but invalid-option class handling is still incomplete for missing-value options.

issues.description: `--path-to-ignore` (and short `-p`) does not enforce a required argument (`let _val = iter.next()`), so `rust-ag --path-to-ignore` falls through and emits `ERR: What do you want to search for?` (no usage on stdout) instead of the baseline invalid-option class diagnostic. Baseline `ag --path-to-ignore` reports option-requires-argument on stderr and usage on stdout. This violates the feature requirement for invalid-option diagnostic class/channel parity and no-silent-fallback behavior.
VAL-CLI-009 tests only cover unknown-option forms (`--invalid-fake-option`, `-Z`) and miss missing-value invalid-option cases, which allowed the `--path-to-ignore` class mismatch to slip through.

sharedStateObservations.observation: Shared-state docs state parity compares stdout/stderr/exit, but the parity runner currently computes output parity from stdout only (with exit code), while stderr is captured but not compared. This can mask channel-specific diagnostic mismatches for contracts like VAL-CLI-009.
sharedStateObservations.evidence: .factory/library/architecture.md:15 says parity compares stdout/stderr/exit; scripts/parity/run_matrix.py:637,692,713 normalizes/compares stdout only (baseline_result["stdout"], target_result["stdout"], output_match = baseline_norm == target_norm).

summary: Feature is close, but it misses a blocking invalid-option parity case: missing argument for `--path-to-ignore`/`-p` is misclassified and does not match baseline diagnostic channel behavior.
